reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 discusses general HEA stability and short-range order but not Cu segregation or premelting. E2 describes noble-metal shell formation in a different alloy system under corrosive conditions, not thermal premelting. E3 shows no long-range ordering in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles and only weak Cu-Mo repulsion, contradicting the claim of strong Cu surface segregation. E4 demonstrates structural stability without elemental segregation in a different HEA (Ru-based) up to 873 K, which does not support the proposed Cu-driven premelting mecha
premises: Cu has a lower melting point than the other HEA constituents, driving preferential surface segregation
Enhanced surface diffusion in the premelting regime causes Cu to migrate to the nanoparticle surface
A Cu-rich surface layer forms a liquid-like layer below the bulk melting point, initiating progressive melting
Pre-annealing homogenization can suppress Cu segregation and delay premelting
